The macro's pins: Di0 north (Metal2), Do0 west, the controls east (Metal3), as the sky130 chip's.  The tile's stripes are run over the macro's power pins by flow.py's Tile.ExtendPowerStripes (odb_stripes.py) after pdn_macro.tcl; src/RAM32.v stays a model for lint (EXTRA_VERILOG_MODELS).

GPL_CELL_PADDING 2 and PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT 72 (the sky130 chip's recipe: 2 and 85): a site each side of every cell in global placement - GF180's cells average 6.9 um here, so +16% - reserves the room the flow's buffers, CTS and hold fixes take afterwards, which otherwise packed bins past 90% where the detailed router stalled.  The target is a little above the padded utilization at placement, so the cells spread over the whole area instead of leaving the far corner empty (Ken, on gf1: empty regions beside the macro while the rest squeezed): without the TTLC the core logic is 452K um2 synthesized (575.4K less the RAM32's flops), 481K at global placement with the fanout buffers, 52% of the 929K um2 beside the macro, about 60% padded (GPL prints its minimum feasible density); the repair, CTS and hold buffers then add about 40% in the room the padding kept.  gf1, the 4x4 with the TTLC at 85 unpadded: 77% utilization, global-route overflow 24632, the detailed router at 33.7K violations after three iterations (stopped).
The antenna repair's iterations as the sky130 chip's rc22+ (3 left a met3 net at 1.02 there).
FP_PRUNE_THRESHOLD: row stubs shorter than this many sites are dropped (pdngen cannot strap them, PDN-0179); the 36-site stubs between the macro and the core's right edge stay.

PDN_CFG: LibreLane's PDN plus a Metal4 stripe (with pdngen's vias to the rails) on each macro power pin column that is not on a tile stripe (none, on the stripe grid); Tile.ExtendPowerStripes then runs the columns over the macro.
